content.text: That's right. As you well know, we started this series. It's a ten-part series and today we're going to talk about sales and charts and graphs and more or less explaining maybe a PowerPoint presentation.

content.text: That's right. So you're going to learn some wonderful ways of talking about changes in markets and marketing. So let's take a listen to today's dialogue and we'll be back in a moment to talk about what you've heard.

content.text: As all of you are well aware, competition in the laptop computer sector is intense. We continue to fight with our competitors for market share and this is the case both in the developed markets in the West as well as more developing markets in Asia and Africa.
content.trans: 英语：众所周知，笔记本电脑市场竞争激烈。我们继续与竞争对手竞争市场份额，并且在西欧和亚洲、非洲等地都如此。

content.text: You may ask yourself, why is this market so cutthroat? Well, the answer is simple. There is a huge untapped potential market out there with a huge untapped potential for profit.
content.trans: 英语：它可能问自己，为什么这个市场这么竞争激烈？嗯，答案很简单。那里有一个巨大的未开发潜力的市场，一个巨大的潜在利润空间。

content.text: If I bring up the first graph here, it shows the increase in terms of number of computer owners across the globe. As you can see in the 1980s, computer ownership amounted to around 0.5% of the total world population.
content.trans: 如果我在这里提到来自全球的计算机拥有量，那么可以看到在1980年代，计算机拥有量占世界人口总数的约0.5%。

content.text: Since the 1990s, computer ownership has risen dramatically. In the new millennium, we saw an even larger explosion in computer owners with figures rising to around 4% to 5%, in increase of 1000% compared with the 1980s.
content.trans: 英语：自1990年代以来，计算机拥有率急剧上升。在新世纪的十年间，我们见证了计算机拥有量从约4%到5%，增加了1000倍于1980年代。

content.text: If we move on to discuss the figures for China specifically, we can see in chart B that the overall figure for computer ownership stands at around 60 million, which represents a huge increase in a very short time period.
content.trans: 如果我们将讨论中国计算机所有权的整体情况从图表B中移开，我们可以看到，在整体上，中国计算机拥有率约为6000万，这表明在过去的一段时间内发生了巨大的变化。

content.text: Now of course, 60 million is just a drop in the ocean if you compare the total population of China. And this is a key reason why the personal computer market is such a hot market.
content.trans: 现在当然，60亿只是沧海一粟之比，这也是中国个人电脑市场如此火热的原因之一。

content.text: For us at Alpha and of course for all of our competitors as well, we have millions of potential customers who are looking to join the internet generation.
content.trans: 英文：对于Alpha和我们的竞争对手来说，我们有数百万潜在客户，他们正在寻找加入互联网世代的机会。

content.text: If we do this right, we really can reap huge rewards in a very short time frame.
content.trans: 如果我们做得很好，那么在短时间内就能获得巨大的回报。

content.text: I now like to move on to discuss the X420 brand itself and compare and contrast with some of our key competitors.
content.trans: 我现在想转而讨论一下X420品牌本身，并与一些我们的主要竞争对手进行比较和对比。

content.text: Alright, we're back. So now let's start with language takeaway.
content.trans: 好的，我明白了。现在让我们从语言取向开始吧。

content.text: Language takeaway.
content.trans: 语言总结。

content.text: Okay, so in the first part of what Mr. Ford is saying, he mentioned something called market share. Now, Margot, what is market share?
content.trans: 好的，现在请继续。

content.text: That's right. Everyone is competing for market share. And this is basically a small portion of your available market. So for example, if you sell perfumes, women's perfume, then your market shares may be women who are 18 to 35 years old in your city or in your town or in your country.
content.trans: 是的，你说得对。每个人都在竞争市场份额。而且这基本上是你可用市场的一部分。例如，如果你卖香水，女性香水、女士香水，那么你的市场份额可能是在你所在的城市或国家的18到35岁的女性中。

content.text: Right. So when we're talking about market share because we're sharing a piece of this big pie, we're going to talk about that in terms of a percentage. So 30% or 15%.
content.trans: 正确。当我们谈论市场份额，因为我们共享这个大蛋糕时，我们将用百分比来讨论这一点。所以30%或15%，等等。

content.text: That's right. I think maybe one of the clearest examples is Coca-Cola has, I think maybe a 60% market share of the carbonated beverages market.
content.trans: 是的，我认为可能有一款饮料品牌，比如可口可乐，它的市场份额大约为60%。

content.text: Interesting. So you could say that Apple has a 50% market share of the personal computing industry.
content.trans: 很好，我已准备好。请问您需要翻译的英文句子是什么？

content.text: That's right. Very good. So this is when what we refer to as market share. Now, as we continue to talk about markets, we have two very interesting words when we refer to a developed market and a developing market.
content.trans: 正确。很好。因此，当我们继续谈论市场时，我们有两个非常有趣的词，当我们将一个成熟的市场和一个发展的市场联系起来。

content.text: Okay. So a developed market is something that has been polished and grown over time. Perhaps we talk about the developed world being Western Europe and America.
content.trans: 好的。那么，一个成熟的市场就是指经过时间的打磨和成长而变得成熟了的东西。或许我们可以谈论一下西方欧洲和美国等发达市场的现状。

content.text: But then we have developing markets and those are markets that are still trying to figure out kind of what's going on. They're growing. They're usually growing much faster than a developed market.
content.trans: 但是然后我们有发展市场，这些市场还在努力理解发生的事情。他们通常比一个成熟市场增长得更快。

content.text: That's right. So again, when we're talking about maybe computers, we consider for example the United States a developed market.
content.trans: 英语：那对了。所以，当我们谈论可能的电脑市场时，我们可以考虑美国作为一个发展中的市场。

content.text: Many people already have a computer or express the desire by one. And so maybe a developing market are some of the African countries where they're still growing. And so now they're beginning to purchase more and more computers.
content.trans: 许多人都已经拥有一台电脑或表达了购买的意愿。而且，也许在非洲的一些发展中国家，他们仍然在成长。现在，他们已经开始购买更多的电脑了。

content.text: Okay. So developed and developing two different ways to describe markets. That's right. Now after that, we hear this phrase cutthroat. So someone asks, why is this market so cutthroat? What does this mean?
content.trans: 好的。所以开发和发展的两种方式来描述市场。这就是正确的。现在，当我们听到“市场如火如荼”时，有人问这是什么意思？这表示什么含义？

content.text: A cutthroat business or a cutthroat industry. It means that it's very, very competitive.
content.trans: 英语：一个竞争激烈的行业或公司。它意味着非常激烈的竞争。

content.text: Okay. So cutthroat, we're actually talking about maybe having a knife and cutting someone else's throat, but it's just a metaphor. It's a way of saying yes, this is very competitive. So you're not actually cutting someone's throat.
content.trans: 好的。所以，我们正在讨论是否应该有刀和切断别人喉咙的手段，但这只是个比喻。它表示是的，这是非常竞争的。所以，你并不切别人喉咙。

content.text: Right. Everyone is fighting for that market share. So it's very cutthroat. Everyone is fighting very, very hard. But you're not literally killing someone or cutting their throats.
content.trans: 是的，每个人都在为那个市场份额而战。所以竞争异常激烈。每个人都在拼尽全力，非常拼命。但你不是真的杀害某人或切断他们的喉咙。

content.text: And you could even use this to talk about a sporting event. You could say, you know, it was a cutthroat game.
content.trans: 你还可以用这种方法谈论体育赛事。你可以这么说，你知道，那是个竞争激烈的比赛。

content.text: That's right. That's right. So anything that's very competitive or very close. So to finish off language takeaway when Mr. Ford was towards the end of his presentation, he said that the rewards could be very, very big in a very short timeframe.
content.trans: 是的，没错。那么任何非常竞争或非常接近的情况。所以，在福特先生接近结束演讲时，他说道，奖励可能在短时间内变得非常巨大。

content.text: So when we say the word timeframe, we mean period of time. It's not like, you know, 2 p.m. It's like from from May to June. We have this short timeframe. It's only two months long.
content.trans: 所以当我们说时间框架时，我们指的是时间段。它不像，你知不知道，从5月到6月。我们有这个短时间段。只有两个月长。

content.text: That's right. So timeframe is a window or a period.
content.trans: 是的，你说得对。时间窗口或时间段。

content.text: Mm-hmm. That's right. So this is what he is referring to is that in a very short period or in this period of time, they could make a lot of money at timeframe.
content.trans: 嗯，你说得对。我明白了。那么，这个傻瓜相机在短时间内能赚很多钱吗？

content.text: Right. But how long would a long time frame be? Maybe a couple of years. All right. So you can have a short time frame and a long time frame.
content.trans: 正确。但多久会是一个长时段？也许几年。好的，你可以有短时段和长时段。

content.text: For us at Alpha and of course for all of our competitors as well, we have millions of potential customers who are looking to join the internet generation.
content.trans: 英文：对于Alpha和我们的竞争对手来说，我们有数百万潜在客户，他们正在寻找加入互联网世代的机会。

content.text: If we do this right, we really can reap huge rewards in a very short time frame.
content.trans: 如果我们做得很好，那么在短时间内就能获得巨大的回报。

content.text: I now like to move on to discuss the X420 brand itself and compare and contrast with some of our key competitors.
content.trans: 我现在想转而讨论一下X420品牌本身，并与一些我们的主要竞争对手进行比较和对比。

content.text: Alright, we're back. So as we mentioned, this is just a part of our presentation series.
content.trans: 好的，我明白了。请继续提供需要翻译的英文内容。

content.text: We're going to keep on talking with Mr. Ford as he discusses business and a lot of other very interesting and useful skills for talking in public.
content.trans: 我们将会继续和福特先生讨论商业以及许多其他非常有趣且有用的公共场合交流技巧。

content.text: That's right. So the goal of this series is to help you feel better when you're giving a presentation in English.
content.trans: 好的，我明白了。请继续提供需要翻译的英文内容。

content.text: We all know it's very, very hard to talk in English when you're when you're still learning, but it's even harder to talk alone to give us speech or presentation.
content.trans: 我们都知道，当我们还在学习的时候，很难用英语流畅地交流。然而，当我们独自讲话或做演示时，更是难上加难。

content.text: And so the point of this series is to really give you those skills and to help teach you some of the key phrases and words that you'll be using in your presentations in the future.
content.trans: 这个系列的目的是让你真正掌握这些技能，并帮助你在未来的演讲中学习和使用一些你将在未来工作中使用的关键术语。

content.text: That's right. So if you have any questions or any doubts, we are always available at English.com. And we'll see everyone there.
content.trans: 是的，您说得对。如果您有任何疑问或疑虑，请随时联系我们：www.english.com。我们将在这里等待您的到来。

content.text: Bye.
content.trans: 再见。
